problems.problem: The delivered template is BROKEN on the target hardware's actual TTS path. Its frontmatter ships Block A 'design mode' (voice_control + voice_seed, no ref_wav). But voice_control is a VoxCPM2-only concept: tts_setup_kwargs() raises ValueError unless tts.backend == 'voxcpm2' (the 4090/CUDA path), and the M5 Max config uses tts.backend: qwen3 (mlx-audio). In the qwen3 branch, render_s2s_argv unconditionally emits str(persona['ref_wav']) and persona['ref_text'] with no None guard.
problems.evidence: ./ref-VoxEMW/voxemw/pipeline/args.py:51-59 — `if tts.get("backend") == "qwen3": ... "--qwen3_tts_ref_audio", str(persona["ref_wav"]), "--qwen3_tts_ref_text", persona["ref_text"]`. I ran the real load_config + render_s2s_argv against the template with configs/assistant.yaml and got literally: `--qwen3_tts_ref_audio None --qwen3_tts_ref_text None`. Confirms the Mac pipeline gets the string "None" as a wav path. Separately, args.py:120-122 `tts_setup_kwargs` raises `ValueError(f"不支持的 tts.backend")` for anything but voxcpm2, so voice_control is never read on Mac.

problems.problem: The headline verification claim is invalid for the target platform. The finding says the template is 'verified working against the real loader' and cites tests/test_config.py::test_load_config_voice_control_without_ref as authority for ref_wav=None being accepted. That test hard-codes `tts: { backend: voxcpm2 }` — the CUDA backend. The qwen3/MLX branch is only ever tested with a persona that HAS ref_wav. There is zero test coverage for the exact configuration the template ships.
problems.evidence: ref-VoxEMW/tests/test_config.py:62-75 — the cited test's config block is `tts: {{ backend: voxcpm2, model_name: openbmb/VoxCPM2 }}`. ref-VoxEMW/tests/test_pipeline_args.py:36,42,77 — the qwen3 argv test supplies `"ref_wav": "/abs/demo/ref.wav"`; lines 149-153 exercise ref_wav=None only through tts_setup_kwargs, i.e. only the voxcpm2 path. The verification stopped at parse_persona_file, the shallowest of the three functions, and never reached the one that breaks.

problems.problem: The memory estimate is wrong by 10-20x and is arithmetic, not measurement. The finding states '~0.02-0.05 GB' and 'tens of megabytes for a 7-14B model at typical head dimensions'. Real KV cache for a 4-6k prefix at those exact dimensions is 0.3-1.0 GB.
problems.evidence: KV bytes = 2(K,V) x layers x kv_heads x head_dim x 2 bytes x tokens. Qwen3-8B (36L, 8 KV heads, 128 dim): 0.59 GB @4k, 0.89 GB @6k. Qwen3-14B (40L): 0.66 / 0.98 GB. Llama-3.1-8B (32L): 0.52 / 0.79 GB. Even the small-head MoE case (gpt-oss-120b class, 36L/8kv/64d) is 0.30 / 0.44 GB. Nothing in the 7-14B GQA family lands anywhere near 20-50 MB. Impact on 128 GB is still negligible, but the number was estimated rather than computed, which is the pattern the review was asked to catch.

problems.problem: The 'per-turn contribution: effectively ZERO' verdict rests entirely on an unverified prefix-cache assumption, in a stack whose shipped brain is a REMOTE API and whose local-LLM option was explicitly abandoned. The finding invokes 'llama.cpp --cache-reuse or the MLX equivalent' — neither is present in this repo.
problems.evidence: configs/assistant.yaml:38-48 sets `llm.backend: chat-completions`, `base_url: https://api.deepseek.com`, model deepseek-v4-flash, with the author's own comment at line 36-38: '本地 8B 脑实测回复质量不达标，已彻底弃用并删除' (local 8B brain measured as below quality bar, completely abandoned and deleted). README.md:3 and scripts/start_mac.sh:2 both state '大脑走 DeepSeek API，本地不跑 LLM'. args.py:83-90 shows the mlx-lm branch passes only `--llm_device` — no cache flag whatsoever. So on the shipped config the ~4k prompt plus a chat_size:30 window is re-uploaded every turn to a network endpoint; on the local mlx-lm branch nothing in this repo establishes cross-turn KV reuse. The finding lists this as an open question yet still stamps 'works-native-fast' and 'effectively ZERO'.

problems.problem: The two sections named as the template's key differentiators (Section 9 concession ladder, Section 11 difficulty governor) are enforced by asking the model to count its own turns — under a rolling 30-message window that evicts the evidence, and with barge-in rewriting the context mid-stream. This is the single least reliable enforcement mechanism available, and the finding never examines it; it worries only about whether the ladder CONTENT is authentic.
problems.evidence: Template Section 9: 'after the user lands a genuinely strong point, you may not go more than two turns without reaching rung 4 on that thread.' Section 11: 'drop one band for three turns'. Section 9 rung 3: 'Legal ONCE per topic.' Against: configs/assistant.yaml:47 `chat_size: 30` (rolling window — early turns fall out of context, taking the counter's evidence with them), and gateway/orchestrator.py docstring lines 15-17: on barge-in the orchestrator writes the heard prefix back into context ('把已听前缀补写回上下文（heard_prefix）'), mutating the very history the model would have to count. The finding's own note that debate turns are longer than the witch's means MORE barge-ins, hence more rewrites.

problems.problem: Section 0's mandatory disclosure directly violates Section 2's 8-word first-sentence rule, on the one turn that also pays the full cold prefill. The finding presents the 8-word cap as 'the one per-turn lever this component owns' running 'strongly in our favour' and never notices its own template defeats it on turn 1.
problems.evidence: Template Section 0 mandates verbatim: 'Quick note first — I'm an AI arguing as <Full Name>, from his public record. Not him. Right — <opening line>.' With configs/assistant.yaml:46 `stream_batch_sentences: 1`, TTS receives sentence #1 the moment it completes — and sentence #1 here is ~15 words / ~20 tokens, not 8. That same first turn is also the one paying the uncached prefill. First-turn time-to-first-audio is therefore the system's worst case, and the finding never sums these; it accounts only for '~3 seconds of the first turn' of speaking time.

problems.problem: The 'belt and braces' evidence claim is FALSE on the target hardware. strip_stage_directions() is wired only into the VoxCPM2 handler, which backends.py registers only when tts.backend == 'voxcpm2'. On the M5 Max qwen3/mlx-audio path there is NO code backstop — the prompt rule is the only defense. The finding cites this as strong evidence that the persona rule is safely redundant; on this machine it is load-bearing and alone.
problems.evidence: Definition at voxemw/pipeline/launch.py:101 (not tts_voxcpm2.py:101 as claimed); sole call site is voxemw/pipeline/tts_voxcpm2.py:103. voxemw/pipeline/backends.py:61 gates registration: `if tts_cfg.get("backend") == "voxcpm2":`. The qwen3 TTS backend is upstream-builtin and never passes through strip_stage_directions. The finding's own risk list predicts the stage-direction ban will be among the first rules a small local model breaks — with the backstop absent, that failure reaches the speaker.

problems.problem: The recommendation never checks whether the hard requirement is met, and the project's own measured numbers say the budget is already at its edge with a persona one-third this size. Tripling the system prompt and moving to a local model has no measurement behind it.
problems.evidence: ref-VoxEMW/docs/plan-4090.md:44-45 budget: 'STT 0.3~0.5s + DeepSeek ~0.6s + VoxCPM2 TTFA ~0.3~0.5s + SoulX 首帧 ~0.3s + 网络 RTT ≈ 1.5~2.2s'. README.md:3 headline: '说完 ~3s 开口' (~3s to speak after you finish). README.md:91 measured on 4090: short-sentence first audio ~1.9s. docs/upgrade-regression.md:39-41, Mac path: '闭嘴→首音 ~2-2.5s 基线' (mouth-closed-to-first-audio ~2-2.5s baseline). All of that is with mojingnvwu.md, whose body I measured at 2,651 chars ≈ ~1,325 tokens. The template is ~3,800-4,300 tokens — roughly 3x — and the finding asserts zero marginal cost without a single measurement on the M5 Max.

problems.problem: The subject is effectively determined by the project directory (distillCKirk → Charlie Kirk), yet the finding defers it to an open question and writes the risk as 'a real, possibly living, person'. If the subject is who the directory name indicates, he is deceased — assassinated in September 2025 — which changes the ethical analysis materially, and the timing (today is 2026-09-09) is the eve of the one-year anniversary. Compounding this: because design mode is broken on Mac (problem 1), the ONLY working voice mode on this hardware is clone mode, which requires ref.wav of the real person's actual voice. The finding explicitly flags voice cloning as 'a separate and larger set of issues' and then recommends the configuration that forces it.
problems.evidence: Directory .; template frontmatter field `subject_status: <living public figure | deceased | living non-public>` left as a placeholder; `voice_control: <mid-Atlantic male, ...>` also a placeholder. Risk list text: 'Impersonation of a real, possibly living, person'. Forcing mechanism: config.py:117-127 requires ref_wav OR voice_control, and args.py:51-59 makes voice_control non-functional on qwen3 — so ref_wav (a real voice sample) is the only path that runs. I could not confirm the subject's status via search (session web-search budget exhausted); the user must confirm the identity before any of this proceeds.

problems.problem: The template ships 31,665 chars of author-facing HTML comments that parse_persona_file does NOT strip, and the only defense is a manual regex step in the install instructions that mutates the file in place. Skip step 3 and you inject ~7,900 tokens of instructions-to-the-author as the system prompt.
problems.evidence: voxemw/config.py:49-79 parse_persona_file does no comment stripping — it returns raw markdown body after frontmatter. I ran it on the unstripped template: body = 30,322 chars ≈ ~7,580 tokens. The finding's install_commands step 3 is a destructive in-place `re.sub` on the persona file, so authoring guidance is lost on first ship and must be re-stripped after every edit. No pipeline-side guard exists.

problems.problem: Minor factual slips that reproduce a pattern of citing without re-checking: the strip_stage_directions line reference is wrong, and the token measurement does not reproduce.
problems.evidence: Claimed 'voxemw/pipeline/tts_voxcpm2.py:101 calls strip_stage_directions()' — it is DEFINED at launch.py:101 and CALLED at tts_voxcpm2.py:103; the researcher appears to have merged the two. Claimed strip yields '15,810 chars (~3,950 tokens)'; running their exact regex `re.sub(r'<!--.*?-->\n?','',t,flags=re.S)` on the current file gives 17,152 chars (~4,288 by chars/4, ~3,791 by word count). Claimed 'the stripped body begins correctly at "# 0 · Disclosure and hard boundaries"' — the stripped file begins with the frontmatter `---`. The orchestrator.py:69-85 and assistant.yaml:46/48 citations DO check out exactly.

problems.problem: The finding under-hedges in one direction and over-hedges in another on the arXiv citation. It flags 2605.23899 as possibly fabricated; the ID is in fact correct. But nuwa's paraphrase of it — which the finding repeats — misdescribes the result.
problems.evidence: arXiv 2605.23899 resolves to 'From Raw Experience to Skill Consumption: A Systematic Study of Model-Generated Agent Skills', which is the SkillLens project (microsoft.github.io/SkillLens confirms arXiv ID 2605.23899). So the citation is sound and the researcher's hedge was over-cautious. However the 46.4% measures an independent LLM judge comparing two skills pairwise — 'An LLM judge asked to compare two skills picks the better one only 46.4% of the time' — not a model self-evaluating its own output. And the paper's own remedy is a validated 3-dimension rubric (46.4% → 73.8%), i.e. the rubric does the work, not necessarily agent separation. nuwa's gloss '自评skill质量准确率仅46.4%' is a misreading the finding inherits.

corrected_recommendation:
Do not ship the template as delivered. Four things must change before it is usable on the M5 Max, and the verdict must drop from "works-native-fast" to "unverified on target hardware".

1. FIX THE VOICE BLOCK (blocking). Delete Block A from the template's frontmatter default, or patch ref-VoxEMW/voxemw/pipeline/args.py:57-58 to guard the qwen3 branch on `persona.get("ref_wav")` the way tts_setup_kwargs already does at args.py:136. As shipped, the Mac pipeline is launched with `--qwen3_tts_ref_audio None`. Then re-verify through load_config + render_s2s_argv, not parse_persona_file — and add the missing test: voice_control-only persona against tts.backend qwen3.

2. MOVE TURN-COUNTED STATE OUT OF THE PROMPT (this is the materially better option the finding missed). Section 9's two-turn concession cap, Section 9 rung 3's "once per topic", Section 11's three-turn difficulty drop, and Section 0's once-per-session disclosure are all counters. Asking a model to count its own turns under `chat_size: 30` with heard_prefix rewrites on every barge-in is the least reliable mechanism available. The orchestrator already owns per-turn context surgery (gateway/orchestrator.py, heard_prefix path) — hold these four counters there and inject a ~10-token per-turn note ("concession_pressure: 2/2 — concede this turn"; "band: B2"; "disclosure: done"). Deterministic, effectively free, and it removes the dominant failure mode of the two sections the recommendation is built around. Do this before building any ledger.

3. RESOLVE THE DISCLOSURE/LATENCY COLLISION. Section 0's mandated sentence is ~15 words and fires as TTS sentence #1 on the turn that also pays cold prefill. Either shorten it to fit the 8-word rule, or have the orchestrator play a pre-rendered disclosure clip at session open while prefill runs — which converts the worst turn in the system into free cover for the prefill.

4. MEASURE BEFORE CLAIMING ZERO. Instrument three things on the actual machine, using the project's own harness: (a) does the chosen local stack reuse the KV prefix across turns as the conversation grows — the entire latency argument is this one assumption and nothing in ref-VoxEMW establishes it; (b) cold prefill wall time for a 4-6k prompt, which the project's own measured 20.0 TFLOPS bf16 (docs/measured-hardware.md) puts nearer 4-15s than "a few seconds"; (c) mouth-closed-to-first-audio against the existing ~2-2.5s Mac baseline (docs/upgrade-regression.md:41) with the 4k persona versus the 1.3k witch. Restate memory as 0.3-1.0 GB of KV, not 0.02-0.05 GB.

Also: confirm the subject's identity and status with the user before any research spend. The directory name points at a specific figure whose status the template leaves as a placeholder and the finding describes as "possibly living". If he is deceased — and if the target is who the directory indicates, he is — the ethical framing changes, and because design mode is broken on this hardware the only runnable voice path is a clone built from his real recorded voice. That is a decision for the user to make explicitly, not a side effect of a broken frontmatter default.

What to keep: the research pipeline recommendation (nuwa for Phase 1, the 7th adversarial agent, split answering/grading agents), the ledger-as-structure argument, the 8-word opener rule, and the template's prose. The document is a good draft. It is not verified, and it does not currently run.
surviving_claims: The persona markdown body IS the system prompt — injected verbatim with no wrapper, summariser, or RAG. Verified exactly: gateway/orchestrator.py:69-85 defines build_session_update with `"instructions": persona_text` at line 77, and its only production call site is orchestrator.py:346 inside _apply_persona. config.py:49-79 parse_persona_file returns the raw post-frontmatter body as `text`. The budgeting argument that follows from this is correct.

assistant.yaml:46 `stream_batch_sentences: 1` and assistant.yaml:48 `reasoning_effort: "none"` are exactly as cited, including the author's comment that the thinking model burns ~2s before speaking. The inference that the first-sentence-length rule is a latency mechanism rather than a style preference is sound.

The 8-word opener latency saving is defensible and if anything UNDERSTATED. Against the project's own measured M5 Max baseline (docs/measured-hardware.md: 426 GB/s effective bandwidth, 60-90 tok/s expected for a ~5B-active MoE, 20-25 tok/s for ~22B-active), 40-48 saved tokens is 0.44-0.80s on the fast case and 1.6-2.4s on the slower one. This is the one quantitative claim in the finding that survives intact.

github.com/alchaincyf/nuwa-skill is real (32,299 stars, created 2026-04-05, default branch main) and references/fidelity-scorecard.md says precisely what is claimed: 5 dimensions to 100 (stance consistency 30, style distinctiveness 20, edge honesty 20, source transparency 15, structural completeness 15), grades A>=85 / B 70-84 / C 55-69 / D<55, and the verbatim anti-cheat rule '答题agent和评分agent必须是两个独立agent，绝不自评自证'.

references/extraction-framework.md's three-way mental-model filter is quoted accurately: 跨域复现 (recurrence across >=2 domains), 有生成力 (predicts stance on new questions), 有排他性 (not what every smart person would think), with 1-of-3 demoting to a decision heuristic and 0-of-3 discarded. Reusing this test to select rhetorical MOVES rather than opinions is a legitimate adaptation.

titanwings/colleague-skill does redirect to titanwings/distilly (24,453 stars, 'Formerly Colleague Skill（原同事 Skill）', last push 2026-09-06), so the provenance claim and the layered-priority/correction-loop characterisation check out.

arXiv 2605.23899 is a real paper and IS the SkillLens work — the researcher's hedge was over-cautious. Its 46.4% figure is real, though it measures a pairwise LLM judge rather than self-evaluation. The underlying practice (do not let a model grade its own roleplay) stands regardless.

The core methodological argument is right and is the most valuable part of the finding: converting 'don't hallucinate' into 'only assert rows from this table' is a structurally stronger instruction than a prohibition, and a debate persona needs its adversarial engine stated explicitly or helpfulness training sands it into agreement. The recommendation to use nuwa for the RESEARCH phase and pour results into a voice-shaped template — rather than using nuwa's own text-advisor skill-template.md — is correct.

The alternatives section is honest and well-reasoned. In particular the rejection of few-shot-transcripts-as-whole-prompt (no control surface, encourages continuation past the record) and the rejection of trump-perspective's analyst-mode default for a voice partner are both right, and the two-model-split analysis correctly identifies that the persona is not what threatens the budget.

The risk list is candid and several items are confirmed by my own checks: prompt-size drift in Sections 6/12, the ledger being a discipline rather than an enforcement mechanism, and the prediction that a small local model will break the turn-length ceiling and the stage-direction ban first. That last one is now MORE serious than stated, since the code backstop is absent on this hardware.
